topic: Al Capone: the Chicago crime boss brought down by income tax

sentences.text: Al Capone ruled Chicago, but income tax put him in prison.
In 1929, seven rival gangsters were murdered, and newspapers named him Public Enemy Number One.
Agents turned to income tax, and charged him with twenty-two counts of evasion.
His own admissions of income became evidence.
Convicted on five counts, he got eleven years.
